flawless (of animals and offerings); of a person or of serving God, 'wholehearted' or 'blameless' by context, with a note at first use
skin disease (mold in cloth and houses), never leprosy
servant or slave by context (note at first use in each book)
law (plural torot 'laws'; a priestly 'torah of X' is 'the procedure for X'; note the sense 'instruction, teaching' at first use in each book)
foreigner who lives among you (a resident foreigner; 'foreigner' alone when the context is clear)
the place the LORD will choose
sweep the evil out from among you
ghosts of the dead / spirits that know things
nefesh (in 'with all your heart and all your nefesh')
dishonor (the verb itself does not say force or consent; notes give the readings)
outsider (someone outside the priesthood, or a stranger to the family)
foreigner (someone from another nation, as in Ruth 2:10; never 'outsider', which is zar)
officials (record-keepers who passed on orders; not "officers")

the LORD of Armies (note at first use: 'armies' may mean Israel's armies, the angels or the stars; this matches the CSB and WEB 'Yahweh of Armies' and is not drift; the NT transliteration kyrios sabaoth (Romans 9:29; James 5:4) is rendered 'the Lord of Armies')
tsalach (the Spirit of the LORD/God 'on' someone)
nagid (of a leader designated by God)

ruler (Saul and David are 'ruler over the LORD's people', 1 Samuel 9:16; 10:1; 13:14; 25:30; melekh is 'king'; nagid for an official who is not a king is rendered by context, e.g. 'officer in charge', Jeremiah 20:1)
the LORD's anointed (one); 'his anointed' (note the later sense 'messiah' at first use in each book)
visionary (kept distinct from ro'eh 'seer', e.g. 'Gad the visionary', 2 Samuel 24:11; 1 Chronicles 29:29 has seer, prophet and visionary side by side)
worthless (a worthless man, worthless men), as in Deuteronomy 13:13 and Judges 19:22
the LORD, the God of Israel
kana' (Niphal, of a person before God)
humble oneself ("he humbled himself"); of enemies defeated, "be brought low"
temple servants (the 'given ones'; note at first use in each book)
the people of the exile / the exile (the community that came back from Babylon)
Beyond the River (the Persian province west of the Euphrates)

the Sheep Gate, the Fish Gate, the Jeshanah Gate, the Valley Gate, the Dung Gate, the Spring Gate (sha'ar ha'ayin), the Water Gate, the Horse Gate, the East Gate, the Miphkad Gate, the Gate of Ephraim, the Gate of the Guard; places: Serpent Spring ('en hattannin), the King's Pool, the Pool of Shelah, the king's garden, the steps that go down from the City of David, David's tombs, the Warriors' House, the armory, the courtyard of the guard, the Ophel, the upper room at the corner, the Broad Wall, the Tower of the Hundred, the Tower of Hananel, the Tower of the Ovens, the bend in the wall (hammiqtsoa', as in 2 Chronicles 26:9)

My God, remember me for good (the same English at 5:19 and 13:31, which have the same Hebrew); 'remember' (zakhar) is always 'remember' in Nehemiah's prayers (1:8; 5:19; 6:14; 13:14; 13:22; 13:29; 13:31)
the high priest (the title of Ezra–Nehemiah and later books); but Leviticus 21:10, hakkohen haggadol me'echav, is 'The priest who is greater than his brothers'
Sanballat the Horonite / Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite (note on 'servant' at 2:10)
deputies (local officials under the governor; not 'officials', which renders sarim in Ezra and sar in Nehemiah 3)
the fortress at Susa (as in Nehemiah 1:1); Shushan alone is 'Susa'; ha'ir Shushan (Esther 3:15; 8:15) is 'the city of Susa'
pole (note at first use: literally 'tree, wood'; the 'hanging' (talah) was probably impaling or putting a body on show; traditional English 'gallows')
the satraps / the governors / the officials of the provinces
feast (also for Esther's two feasts; mishteh hayyayin 'the wine feast', Esther 5:6; 7:2, 7–8)
Pur, that is, the lot / Purim
sending portions of food to one another
If the king thinks it good (as in Nehemiah 2:5, 7 and Ezra 5:17)
the king's gate (Mordecai sits 'in the king's gate')
eunuchs (note at 1:10 on the sense 'court official')
law / laws ('the laws of Persia and Media', 1:19); devar hammelekh vedato 'the king's word and law' (2:8; 4:3); pitgam (1:20) 'ruling'
the women's house (the second one, 2:14, 'the second women's house')
Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite
to annihilate, kill and destroy (hashmid 'annihilate' and 'abbed 'destroy' kept apart throughout Esther)
And if I perish, I perish ('avad 'perish' also in 4:14)
raise a hand against (to attack, as in 2:21; 3:6); of plunder, 'kept their hands off the plunder' (9:10, 15, 16)
the Accuser (a title with the article, not a personal name; note at first use; 1 Chronicles 21:1 satan without the article is 'Satan')
God (as Elohim and El; notes point out the name where it matters)
ʾƎgziʾä səbḥat (1 Enoch; Greek kyrios tēs doxēs)
nəguś zäläʿaläm (1 Enoch 25; 27; Greek basileus tou aiōnos)
ʿäbiy səbḥat (1 Enoch 14:20; 102:3; Greek hē doxa hē megalē)
the Head of Days (Daniel 7:9's 'Ancient of Days'); 46:1 has the fuller 'one who had a head of days'
the Chosen One (plural ḫəruyan 'the chosen ones', 'the chosen')
wäldä säbʾ / wäldä bəʾəsi / wäldä ʾəgʷalä ʾəmmäḥəyaw (1 Enoch 37–71)

the Son of Man (all three; a note at the first of each in 46:2, 62:7 and 69:29 says which stands there; 62:5 wäldä bəʾəsit is 'Son of a Woman'; a plain address to a human being, as in 60:10, is 'son of man')

family redeemer, for the relative who buys back land or people (Leviticus 25:25; Ruth 2:20; 3:9; 4:1–8); go'el haddam 'the avenger of blood' (Numbers 35:19); 'redeemer' when the go'el is God (Isaiah 41:14) or not named, as in Job 19:25, 'my redeemer' (lowercase in Job, because who is meant is debated; note at 19:25); gloss 'the one who comes to my rescue, as family would'
shepherds (the seventy shepherds; never used for God or Israel's kings in the Animal Apocalypse)
the lights (the sun, moon and stars; never "luminaries")
gate / gates (of the sun, moon, stars and winds); mäsakw 'windows'
the Lord (Ge'ez does not use the name YHWH, so never "the LORD")
Woe to ("Woe to you who..."; never "Alas")
täklä ṣədq (1 Enoch 10:16; 93:2–10; compare täklä zärʾ 'plant of seed' in 84:6)
sänbät (1 Enoch 93:3–10; 91:12–17, the Apocalypse of Weeks)
deep shadow (the 'shadow of death' reading goes in a note)
For the music director (note at first use: the meaning is debated; the Greek has 'for the end')
a psalm / a song / a praise
kept as 'a maskil', 'a miktam', 'a shiggaion', with a note at first use giving the proposed meanings
Selah, kept as a word of its own at the end of the line (note at first use: meaning unknown, probably a musical or liturgical mark)
Happy (as in 'Happy is the one who'; note at first use on 'blessed' in older versions)
Praise the LORD! (note at first use: Hebrew 'Hallelujah', 'praise Yah')
Sheol (gloss at first use in each part: the world of the dead)
alms / give alms (giving to the poor, a person's act of mercy); of God, 'mercy' (Tobit 3:2); gloss at first use in each part: 'gifts to the poor'
what is right / right deeds (plural: 'acts of justice' by context); never 'charity'
Κύριος (Greek books outside the Hebrew Bible: Tobit, Judith, Maccabees, Wisdom, Sirach)
the Lord (the Greek has no divine name, so never 'the LORD'); ὁ ὕψιστος 'the Most High'
Raphael (the narrator's name for the angel) / Azariah (the name he gives Tobit and Tobias, 5:13); Tobias calls him 'Brother Azariah'
orders (found only in the Psalms; KJV 'precepts'; 19:8 and throughout Psalm 119)
saying (plural 'sayings'; often a promise; kept distinct from davar 'word', as in Psalm 12:6 and Psalm 119)
the hill country (the highlands of Judea and Samaria)
ὁ θεὸς τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (Judith; Tobit; Ezra–Nehemiah in Greek)
foreigners (in the Septuagint's histories usually the Philistines, and translated so there)
maid (Judith's personal maid; also called παιδίσκη 'slave girl' and δούλη 'slave')
deceit / deceive (12:16, of Holofernes' intent, 'seduce', with a note giving the shared word)

wisdom / wise (the skill of living well; Lady Wisdom in Proverbs 1:20–33; 8–9 is 'Wisdom' with a capital; 9:1 chokmot, a plural of majesty, is also 'Wisdom'; 14:1 is pointed chakhmot nashim 'the wisest of women', as in Judges 5:29, with the re-pointed 'Wisdom' given as a variant)
discipline (note at 1:2: the word covers instruction, correction and punishment; the verb yasar is 'discipline'; 'correction' only where the context is plainly punishment, with a note)
understanding / understanding (both; where the two stand in one verse, tevunah is 'discernment', as in 2:3; hevin, the verb, is 'understand')
knowledge (the verb yada' 'know'; da'at Elohim 'the knowledge of God', 2:5)

shrewdness / shrewd, in the good sense (1:4; 8:5, 12; 12:16, 23; 13:16; 14:8, 15, 18; 22:3; 27:12); in the bad sense (Genesis 3:1; Exodus 21:14; Job 5:12) 'crafty, cunning', with a note where Proverbs shares the word
discretion, in the good sense (1:4; 2:11; 3:21; 5:2; 8:12); in the bad sense 'schemes' (12:2; 14:17; 24:8 ba'al mezimmot 'a master schemer'); zamam 'plan, scheme' by context
sound wisdom (2:7; 3:21; 8:14; 18:1; as in Job 11:6; 12:16; note at first use: the word also means 'success, what works')
fool (the dull, self-satisfied fool, the commonest fool word; kesilut 'folly' only in 9:13, 'Woman Folly')
stubborn fool / folly (the fool who will not be taught, 1:7; 12:15; 15:5; 27:22; note at 1:7; Job and Psalms, which do not set it beside kesil, render 'evil simply 'fool')
godless fool (the boor who has no regard for God or decency, 17:7, 21; 30:22; compare Psalm 14:1 'the fool' and Job 2:10 'a godless woman'; nevalah 'outrage')
mocker / mockery / mock (the scoffer who sneers at correction, as in Psalm 1:1 'mockers'; 9:7–8; 13:1; 21:24 lets is his name)
naive / the naive / naivety (the untaught, easily led young person, not stupid but open to any influence, as Job 5:2 'the naive'; Psalms 19:7; 116:6; 119:130 have 'the simple', the same word)
righteous (the righteous, a righteous person) / wicked (the wicked, a wicked person); tsedeq and tsedaqah 'what is right' and 'righteousness' by context; resha' 'wickedness'

the strange woman / the foreign woman (zarah is the feminine of zar 'outsider': a woman outside a man's marriage and family; nokhriyyah is the feminine of nokhri 'foreigner'; note at 2:16 on whether she is a real foreigner, an adulteress, or a figure for Folly; never 'adulteress' in the text)
the fear of the LORD (keep 'fear'; note at first use, Proverbs 1:7, on awe, reverence and dread)
proverb / proverbs (also 'saying'; 1:1, 6; 10:1; 25:1; 26:7, 9; melitsah 'figure' or 'puzzling saying' and chidot 'riddles', 1:6)

a woman of strength (Proverbs; chayil is 'strength' also in 31:3 and 'asu chayil 'have done strong things', 31:29; note at 31:10 on 'virtuous', 'noble', 'capable' and 'valor'; Ruth 3:11 keeps its own Plain 'a woman of worth')
beer (as in 20:1; note at first use in each part: mostly grain beer, possibly other fermented drinks, never distilled liquor; 'strong drink' is the traditional English, as in the KJV)
lazy one (in address, 'you lazy one'); otherwise 'the lazy one' or 'a lazy person'; never 'sluggard'; 'atslah 'laziness'
senseless (literally 'lacking heart'; 'a senseless young man', 'the senseless'; note at first use)
teaching, for a parent's or a sage's torah (1:8; 3:1; 4:2; 6:20, 23; 7:2; 13:14; 31:26), as in Psalm 78:1, with a note at 1:8; 'law' where God's law may be meant (28:4, 7, 9; 29:18), with a note
the Citadel (the Seleucid fort in Jerusalem; capital C)
φίλος (τοῦ) βασιλέως / οἱ πρῶτοι φίλοι / συγγενεῖς (1 Maccabees)
Friend of the King / the First Friends / Kinsmen (Seleucid court ranks, capitalized; note at first use)
governor (of a region) or general (in a campaign), by context
Heaven (capital H, with a note: 1 Maccabees avoids the word 'God')
"in the year 160" (the Seleucid era), with the BC date in a note
Hasideans (Hebrew ḥasidim, 'the loyal'; note at first use)
stand good for (a person or a loan: guarantee another's debt); taqa' kaf 'strike palms' (22:26 'clap hands'; 11:15 'the handshake that seals a pledge'), the gesture that sealed the guarantee

vapor / Vapor of vapors (everywhere, never 'meaningless', 'futile' or 'vanity' in the text; hakkol hevel 'everything is vapor'; gam-zeh hevel 'this too is vapor'; note at first use in each part on breath, smoke, 'meaningless', 'vanity' and 'absurd')
Qohelet (a name, always untranslated; note at 1:1 on 'the Gatherer' from qahal 'assembly', 'the Teacher', 'the Preacher' and the Greek Ecclesiastes)
chasing the wind (both forms; 'vapor and chasing the wind'); ruach elsewhere is 'wind', 'spirit' or 'breath' by context, with a note where it matters (3:19–21; 12:7)
under the sun / under the heavens
gain (mah-yitron 'What gain...?'; the related yoter 'more, advantage' by context)
toil (noun and verb: 'all his toil that he toils under the sun')
share (a person's share or portion in life: 2:10, 21; 3:22; 5:18–19; 9:6, 9; 11:2)
what is done / the things that are done (ma'aseh ha'elohim 'what God does' or 'the work of God'; of a person's projects, 'works', as in 2:4, 11)
forever (le'olam 'forever', 1:4; 3:14; le'olamim 'long ages', 1:10; 3:11 ha'olam 'forever', with a full note on 'eternity', 'the world' and 'ignorance' by re-pointing)
task (the busy work God has given people: 1:13; 2:23, 26; 3:10; 4:8; 5:3, 14; 8:16)
fate (what happens to someone in the end, death above all; a note at 2:14 says it is not a planned destiny)
God (Ecclesiastes never uses YHWH; note at first use in each part)
a person, people or humans by context / human beings
'en tov ba'adam sheyyokhal veshatah... tov ba'amalo (Ecclesiastes 2:24; 3:12–13, 22; 5:18; 8:15)

the refrain: 'There is nothing good for a person but to eat and drink and let himself see good in his toil' (2:24); later forms keep the same words where the Hebrew is the same: 'eat and drink and see good in all his toil' (3:13)
season / time (3:1 'Everything has its season'; each line of 3:2–8 'a time to...')
yesh ra'ah ra'iti tachat hashamesh (Ecclesiastes 6:1; 10:5; with cholah 5:13)
'There is an evil I have seen under the sun' (5:13 'There is a sickening evil I have seen under the sun')

Christ as part of a name ('Jesus Christ', 'Christ Jesus') and in the letters; 'the Messiah' where the Gospels and Acts use it as a title with the article ('Are you the Messiah?', 'the Messiah must suffer'); note at first use in each book: Greek for Hebrew mashiach, 'anointed one'
ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ / τῶν οὐρανῶν
the kingdom of God / the kingdom of heaven (keep Matthew's 'of heaven'; note: a Jewish way of saying 'of God'; basileia also means reign, 'God ruling as king')
the Son of Man (capitals as a title of Jesus; 'a son of man' in Revelation 1:13; 14:14 and Daniel 7:13 as there)
Amen, I tell you (John's doubled form: 'Amen, amen, I tell you'); note at first use: Jesus puts 'amen' first, which no one else did
church (the Christian community, local or universal); 'assembly' for Israel in the wilderness (Acts 7:38) and the town meeting of Acts 19:32, 39, 41; note at Matthew 16:18

Lord (of Jesus and of God); 'master' or 'sir' when a slave or stranger speaks; in quotations where the Hebrew has YHWH, 'the Lord' (the Greek has no divine name, so never 'the LORD'), with a note pointing to the Old Testament wording
slave (as in Jude 1:1 and Judith); note at first use in each book: Greek and Roman slavery, and why many English Bibles say 'servant'. διάκονος 'servant'; παῖς 'servant' or 'boy' by context
οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι (Gospel of John and Acts)
the Jews (the Greek word is kept), with a note at each place where it means the Jerusalem authorities or the people of Judea; never 'the Jewish leaders' in the Plain, because that is interpretation
scribes (gloss at first use in each book: 'experts in the law of Moses')
the chief priests / the high priest
repent / repentance (gloss at first use: 'turn your life around')
the good news / tell the good news (note at first use: the word behind 'gospel')
Gehenna, with a note at first use in each book (the Valley of Hinnom, Jeremiah 7:31; the usual English 'hell' hides the place name) and a gloss 'the fire of hell'
Hades (as in Revelation); note: the Greek for Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead
righteousness / righteous (note where 'justice' or 'doing what is right' is meant, such as Matthew 5:6; 6:1)
justify (gloss: 'declare to be in the right'); 'prove right' where wisdom or God is the object (Matthew 11:19; Luke 7:29, 35)
faith / believe (trust by context); πίστις Χριστοῦ is decided in the Paul brief
grace (gloss at first use in each book: 'gift of kindness no one earned'); 'thanks' where it means thanks
flesh (never 'sinful nature'); note where Paul uses it for human nature turned against God
the saints, as in Jude 1:3 (gloss at first use in each book: 'God's holy people')
only, of a son or daughter ('his only son'); in John 1:14, 18; 3:16, 18 'one and only' is avoided: 'the only Son' with a note on 'only begotten' (KJV) and 'unique'
the Advocate (note: also Helper, Comforter, Counselor; a person called to stand beside you)
I am (note on the absolute uses: John 8:24, 28, 58; 13:19; 18:5–8 and Exodus 3:14; Isaiah 43:10)
eternal life (note: literally 'life of the age', the life of the age to come)
tax collectors (gloss at first use: 'tax agents working for Rome's system')
the Pharisees / the Sadducees / the Herodians (note at first use in each Gospel)
hypocrite (note: the word for a stage actor)
the Passover / the Feast of Unleavened Bread (as in the Old Testament)
disciple / apostle (for the office; where ἀπόστολος is a general word for 'someone sent' in a saying, as John 13:16 and 2 Corinthians 8:23, 'one who is sent' or 'messenger', with a note) / the Twelve
love / love / love (show the difference in a note where it matters, as John 21:15–17; do not force 'like' for φιλέω)
the nations (the Gentiles where it means non-Jews as people: 'the Gentiles' in Paul and Acts)
skin disease / a man with a skin disease (as tsara'at in Leviticus; never 'leprosy' or 'leper'); note at first use in each book that it is not modern Hansen's disease
tassel (the tsitsit of Numbers 15:38; never 'hem'; 'fringe' only in a note)

save ('your faith has saved you'), with a gloss 'healed and made whole', so the link with salvation stays visible; the compound διασῴζω in healing stories (Matthew 14:36) is 'made completely well', with the same gloss; elsewhere διασῴζω is 'bring safely through' (Acts 27:44)

the Cananaean (gloss 'the zealous one', lowercase; note: Aramaic qan'ana, 'zealous'; the KJV's 'Canaanite', from the later spelling Κανανίτης, is misleading); Ζηλωτής (Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13) 'the Zealot'
Beelzebul (never the KJV's Latin-derived 'Beelzebub', except when quoting the KJV; gloss 'the prince of demons')
you with so little faith / little faith

the Feast of Booths (Sukkot), as in Leviticus 23:34 and 2 Maccabees; the 7:2 note gives 'Tabernacles'. Why: the lane first chose 'Festival of Shelters', but the published Old Testament uses 'Feast of Booths' everywhere (lead, 2026-10-25). Likewise 'the Feast of Dedication' (John 10:22).

bow down to / bow down before (in every Gospel scene, including 2:2, 4:9–10, 14:33, 28:9, 17), with a note at first use in each book that the same word means 'worship' and that the Gospel leaves the reader to see who deserves it; 'worship' only where no bodily act is in view (John 4:20–24)
The LORD says this (as in Samuel and Kings; 'The Lord GOD says this' for koh amar Adonai YHWH); note at first use in each book: the formula of a messenger delivering a king's words

the LORD declares (as in 2 Kings 19:33; 22:19), at the end of a clause, set off by commas; ne'um Adonai YHWH tseva'ot 'the Lord GOD of Armies declares'; note at first use in each book: ne'um is a noun, 'an utterance of the LORD'

oracle (as in Proverbs 30:1; 'The oracle concerning Babylon', Isaiah 13:1); note at first use in each book: from nasa' 'lift', so 'a lifting up (of the voice)'; KJV 'burden'; Jeremiah 23:33–40 plays on both senses

Woe to (before the people addressed, 'Woe to those who...'); in a funeral lament 'Alas' (1 Kings 13:30); a bare call to attention 'Hey!' or 'Come!' (Isaiah 55:1); note at first use in each book: hoy was the cry at a funeral
the day of the LORD / on that day
the Holy One of Israel (as in 2 Kings 19:22)
Daughter Zion / the virgin, Daughter Zion (as in 2 Kings 19:21 and Psalm 9:14); bat 'ammi 'my dear people' (literally 'the daughter of my people'), with a note at first use
young woman (as in Genesis 24:43; Exodus 2:8; Proverbs 30:19); at Isaiah 7:14 the note, the variant (Greek parthenos) and a traditions card give the 'virgin' reading and Matthew 1:23
my servant / the servant, lower case in the Plain (capitalizing would decide who he is); notes and the topic servant-of-the-lord give the readings

justice / righteousness ('justice and righteousness'); in Isaiah 40–66 tsedeq and tsedaqah often mean God's saving action, 'victory, rescue, vindication': by context, with a note at first use in each part
vision ('The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz', Isaiah 1:1); chazah 'see (in a vision)'
the Chaldeans (as in 2 Kings 25; note at first use in each book: the people of southern Babylonia, whose dynasty ruled Babylon from 626 BC; in Daniel also a class of learned men)
worthless idols (a play on 'elohim 'gods' and 'al 'not': 'nothings'); note at first use in each book

teaching, for the prophet's or the LORD's torah (Isaiah 1:10; 2:3; 5:24; 8:16, 20; 30:9; 42:4, 21, 24; 51:4, 7), as in Proverbs, with a note at 1:10 on the older 'law'; plural torot 'laws' (24:5). Why: in Isaiah torah is spoken instruction from a prophet or from God, parallel to 'the word of the LORD' (1:10; 2:3), and 2:3 plays on yarah 'teach'

the islands ('Islands, be silent before me!', Isaiah 41:1; 'The islands are waiting for his teaching', 42:4): the coastlands and islands of the Mediterranean, and so the far ends of the earth; singular 'i 'island, coast'. A gloss at first use in each part gives the sense 'far coastlands'
Ha! (a threat, where the LORD turns on his foes; hoy is not a lament or a call there; note at the verse)

turn (someone's) fortunes around ('I will turn Moab's fortunes around', 48:47), as in Job 42:10; note at first use in each part: literally 'turn back the turning' or 'bring back the captivity' (KJV, and Deuteronomy 30:3 on this site); the phrase plays on shuv 'turn', Jeremiah's key verb, and means a full reversal, not only a return from exile
Terror all around (as in Psalm 31:13 on this site; Pashhur's new name in 20:3 'Terror All Around'); note at first use in each part: Jeremiah's catchphrase, which his enemies threw back at him (20:10)
the Lord / the Master (as in Judith and Tobit, never 'the LORD'); ὁ παντοκράτωρ 'the Almighty', θεὸς παντοκράτωρ 'God Almighty', as in Judith
the temple (both words); ὁ ἅγιος τόπος 'the holy place'
Judaism (note at first use: the word appears first in 2 Maccabees, as the opposite of Ἑλληνισμός, 4:13; compare Galatians 1:13–14)
way of life / live, govern one's life (the ancestral constitution and customs, 4:11; 8:17)
the Feast of Booths (as in Leviticus 23:34)
ἐπιφάνεια, of God's intervention (2 Maccabees 2:21; 3:24; 5:4; 12:22; 14:15; at 15:27 only in Venetus, where Swete has ἐπιμελείᾳ)
appearance (the notes may say 'manifestation'); Ἐπιφανής, the king's title, is 'Epiphanes'
the Sovereign / sovereign power (capitalized as a title of God; lowercase for human rulers, 9:25; 15:5)
their fathers' tongue (the ancestral language, Hebrew or Aramaic; a note at first use)
the Greek way / foreign ways (Ἑλληνισμός is the opposite of Ἰουδαϊσμός; τὰ Ἑλληνικά 6:9 'the Greek way' too)
the ancestral laws / the laws of our fathers (the legal phrase of royal charters; a note at 7:2)
ὁ φίλος, the court rank (2 Maccabees 7:24; 8:9; 10:13)
a Friend (capitalized as a title: 'one of the king's Friends')
the sacrificial organs / the sacrificial meal (the inner parts eaten at a Greek sacrifice)
ἀνάστασις / ἀνίστημι, of the dead (2 Maccabees 7:9, 14; 12:43–44)
resurrection / raise (never 'rise up' alone for the rising of the dead)
the days of keeping apart (the persecution years, when faithful Jews refused to mix with Gentile ways; the Latin and the KJV at 14:3 reverse it to 'mingling')
wisdom; 'Wisdom' with a capital where she is personified (chiefly 6–10); τεχνῖτις σοφία (14:2) 'a craftsman's wisdom'

spirit (capital S only for God's Spirit, 1:7; 9:17, by context, with a note; 12:1 'your imperishable spirit'); 'breath' where it is the life-breath (2:3; 11:20 'one breath'; 15:11, 16; 16:14); 'wind' at 13:2 and 17:18
λόγος / ῥῆμα, God's; λογισμός (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1; 12:9; 16:12, 26; 18:15, 22)

word (lowercase, even at 18:15 'your all-powerful word', with a note there on John 1:1 and the Christian reading of the Logos; ῥῆμα 16:26 'word' too) / λογισμός 'reasoning' (plural 'reasonings, thoughts')
soul (the Greek sense matters in this book; 16:9 and 16:14 included; a note where 'life' is the sense, e.g. 15:8)
righteous (the righteous, a righteous person) / unrighteous / righteousness (1:1, 15)
ἀφθαρσία / ἄφθαρτος / φθαρτός / φθορά (Wisdom of Solomon)
incorruption / imperishable / perishable / decay (moral 'corruption' by context, 14:12, 25); note at first use in each part
holy ones (ὅσιοι 'your holy ones'; ἅγιοι 18:9 'the saints' would mislead, so 'the holy people', with a note)
Δέσποτα / δεσπότης, of God (Wisdom of Solomon)
παιδεύω / νουθετέω / κολάζω / κόλασις (Wisdom of Solomon)
idol / carved image / object of worship
commander (as John 18:12; gloss or note at first use: a Roman tribune, 'commander of a thousand'); σπεῖρα 'cohort'; ἑκατοντάρχης / ἑκατόνταρχος 'centurion'
barracks (the Antonia fortress; gloss at first use); in Hebrews 13:11, 13 and Revelation 20:9 'camp'
the Sanhedrin (as Matthew 5:22; 26:59), the Jewish high council; topic sanhedrin
the Hellenists / the Hebrews (gloss at first use: Greek-speaking and Aramaic-speaking Jews; note at Acts 6:1 on the readings)
the commander of the temple (as Acts 4:1; gloss: the priest in charge of the temple police); his ὑπηρέται 'guards' (as John 7:32; 18:3)
Founder (as Acts 3:15 'the Founder of life'; 5:31 'Founder and Savior'), with a note on 'leader, prince, pioneer'
builder (a craftsman in wood and stone; note at first use that the traditional English is 'carpenter'); Matthew 13:55 'the builder's son', Mark 6:3 'the builder'
John the Baptist (the noun, Matthew; Mark 6:25; 8:28) / John the Baptizer (Mark's participle, 1:4; 6:14, 24), so the reader can see Mark's variation
synagogue leader (gloss at first use: a local leader who ran the meetings)
act of power / acts of power (as Matthew 11:20–23; 13:54, 58; Mark 6:2, 5); gloss 'miracles'

overseer (note at first use in each book: the word behind English 'bishop'; in Acts 20:17, 28 and Titus 1:5–7 the same leaders are called elders); πρεσβύτεροι of church leaders 'elders'; ἐπισκοπή is 'charge' or 'office' where it means a position, not a person (Acts 1:20 'his charge')

judgment seat in Acts and Paul's letters (gloss or note at first use: the raised platform where a Roman official heard cases); exception Acts 12:21 'platform', where Herod speaks from it; in Acts 7:5 'a foot of ground'. Matthew 27:19 'the judge's bench' and John 19:13 'the judge's platform' were published before this entry and are not governed by it; the lead may align them at publish.
proconsul (gloss at first use: the Roman governor of a senatorial province)
οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν / οἱ σεβόμενοι (τὸν θεόν) / προσήλυτος (Acts 10:2, 22; 13:16, 26, 43, 50; 16:14; 17:4, 17; 18:7)

those who fear God / those who worship God (Gentile sympathizers of the synagogue; gloss at first use in each part: 'non-Jews who worship Israel's God') / proselyte (a full convert to Judaism; gloss 'convert to Judaism'); note at 13:16 on the God-fearers debate
common / unclean (both kept, as the Acts brief fixes for Peter's vision: 'What God has made clean, you must not call common'); κοινόω 'call common' or 'make common' by context
Christian (in quotation marks at Acts 11:26, where the name is new; note there on the Latin-style ending and who coined it)

alms / give alms (as Acts 3:2–3 and the Septuagint term for Tobit; 10:2 'He gave much in alms to the people'); gloss at first use in each part 'gifts to the poor'. Matthew 6:2–4 renders the phrase 'give to the poor', which stays as it is

tongues (of fire, Acts 2:3) / speak in tongues (the gift: Acts 10:46; 19:6; 1 Corinthians 12–14), with a gloss and the topic spiritual-gifts; but 'speak in other languages' at Acts 2:4 and 'our own languages' at 2:11, where Luke says the hearers understood them in their native languages (διάλεκτος 'native language', 2:6, 8); the 2:4 note gives the shared word
the Nazarene ('Jesus the Nazarene', as Matthew 26:71 and John 18:5; 'Jesus Christ the Nazarene', Acts 3:6; 4:10); Ναζαρηνός (Mark) also 'the Nazarene'; 'the sect of the Nazarenes' (Acts 24:5)
παῖς, of Jesus and of David (Acts 3:13, 26; 4:25, 27, 30; Matthew 12:18)
servant ('his servant Jesus', 'your holy servant Jesus', 'your servant David'), with a note at Acts 3:13 on Isaiah 52:13 and the KJV's 'Son' or 'child'
δεσπότης / Δέσποτα, of God (Luke 2:29; Acts 4:24; Revelation 6:10)

Master (as for God in Judith, 2 Maccabees and Wisdom); of Christ in Jude 1:4 and 2 Peter 2:1 as there; distinct from ἐπιστάτης, also 'Master' (Luke's word for Jesus as the disciples' leader); glosses name the Greek word where both occur
ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, of the believers (Acts 1:15; 2:1, 44, 47; 1 Corinthians 11:20; 14:23)
together / in one place / in the same place by context; Acts 2:47 'to the gathering' (the Byzantine 'to the church' is a variant)

freedom of speech / freely / speak freely (Acts 2:29 'speak freely'; 4:13 'speak so freely'); where danger is present, pair freedom with courage rather than 'boldness' alone (4:29 'with complete freedom and courage'; 4:31 'freely and fearlessly'); 'boldly' may stand for παρρησιάζομαι in narrative (9:27–28); 28:31 'with complete freedom to speak'; note at Acts 4:13
your holy one (lowercase; the Greek of the Psalm), with a note that the site's Psalm 16:10, from the Hebrew chasid, reads 'your loyal one'

Master (Luke's own word for Jesus, used where Mark has 'Rabbi' or 'Teacher'; distinct from δεσπότης 'Master', said of God at Luke 2:29 and Acts 4:24, so a gloss at first use, Luke 5:5, names the Greek word, and the note there explains the difference)
lake (Luke's word for the Lake of Galilee, where Matthew and Mark say 'sea'; Luke 5:1 'Lake Gennesaret')

lawyer / the lawyers (experts in the Law of Moses, Luke's usual word where Mark and Matthew say 'scribes'; gloss at first use in each part: 'experts in the Law of Moses, not courtroom lawyers'); kept distinct from γραμματεῖς 'scribes'. Titus 3:13 (Zenas the νομικός) is left out: he may have been a Torah expert or a Roman jurist

sanctuary (ναός, the holy building itself, which only priests entered: Matthew 27:51; Mark 15:38; Luke 1:9, 21–22) / temple (ἱερόν, the whole complex with its courts, where crowds gathered and Jesus taught: Luke 2:27, 46; 19:45–47) in Matthew, Mark, Luke and Acts; note at first use in each book. John keeps its own published decision: ἱερόν 'temple grounds', ναός 'temple' (John 2:14–21). Pagan ναοί are 'shrines' (Acts 17:24). 2 Maccabees keeps 'temple' for both. Lowercase 'temple' in all prose. Why: already the practice in Matthew and Mark, and Luke and Acts keep it; John was published first, and its wordplay at 2:19–21 ('Tear this temple down ... the temple of his body') reads naturally only with 'temple', so John's notes explain the Greek there instead.

wealth (as Matthew 6:24; note at first use in each book: Aramaic mamona, 'wealth, property', the KJV's 'mammon', not the name of a demon); Luke 16:9, 11 μαμωνᾶς τῆς ἀδικίας / ὁ ἄδικος μαμωνᾶς 'the wealth of dishonesty' / 'dishonest wealth'
κόλπος, of reclining at a meal (John 1:18; 13:23; Luke 16:22–23)
embrace (as John 1:18 'the Father's embrace' and John 13:23; Luke 16:22 'Abraham's embrace', with a gloss on the place of honor at a feast; KJV 'bosom', other versions 'side')

sensible (good sense: Matthew 7:24; 24:45; 25:2; Luke 12:42 'faithful and sensible'); shrewd / shrewdly where it means worldly cleverness (Luke 16:8, with a note linking 12:42); Matthew 10:16 'sharp' (snakes)
